09:00.headline: Pitchers: it's not just velo
09:00.topic: What college coaches evaluate in a pitcher beyond velo: projection, strikes, repeatable delivery, competitiveness
09:00.caption:
Does your player's velo tell the whole story?

It's usually the first number coaches ask about. It's rarely the only thing they write down.

When college coaches evaluate a high school pitcher, they're also watching:

⚾ Where his velo is headed, not just where it is today
⚾ Whether he throws strikes, especially when he's behind in the count
⚾ A delivery he can repeat pitch after pitch
⚾ How he competes after a walk, an error or a hard-hit ball

Velo opens the conversation. Strikes and composure help keep it going.

A good first step: know where his velo sits compared with typical ranges at D1, D2, D3, NAIA and JUCO.

See what the numbers say about your player's best fit:

13:00.headline: What he does between pitches
13:00.topic: Coaches evaluate body language and makeup: hustle, supporting teammates, reaction to strikeouts and umpires
13:00.caption:
What does your player do when the ball isn't in play?

Coaches watch more than at-bats. Between pitches and between innings, they see how a player carries himself.

✅ Does he hustle on and off the field?
✅ Does he pick up a teammate after a mistake?
❌ Does he sulk after a strikeout?
❌ Does he argue balls and strikes with the umpire?

None of this shows up in a box score or on a radar gun. But it's part of the picture a coach forms, and it's something your player controls every single game.

His numbers can help get a coach to the field. His body language is part of what that coach sees once he's there.
